description:
FILED s526w2 (Opus, 2026-10-24), Pod-Simple-3.47 board census.  PRE-EXISTING on main b89b6add.  LOUD (dies).

    print "[@Foo::ISA] [@Bar::ISA]\n";
    package Foo; use base "File::Spec";
    package Bar; BEGIN { push our @ISA, "File::Spec" }
  perl: [File::Spec] [File::Spec]     PCL: [] [File::Spec]

    BEGIN { package MyX; use base "Pod::Simple::XHTML"; sub start_code { 1 } }
    print "isa=@MyX::ISA\n"; my $p = MyX->new;
  perl: isa=Pod::Simple::XHTML, MyX    PCL: isa= , dies "Can't locate object method "new" via package "MyX""

    my $p = Blurb->new;  package Blurb; use base qw/Pod::Simple::Methody/;
    sub new { my $n = shift->SUPER::new(@_); $n }
  perl: Blurb   PCL: dies (Blurb's @ISA is still empty when SUPER::new resolves; the CLOS defclass the preamble emits gives the DIRECT parent, but Methody reaches Pod::Simple::new only through Methody's own @ISA)

WHERE: Pl/Parser.pm _process_use_base emits `(p-push $isa_sym "Parent")` in the RUN-TIME stream (the require-parent / defpackage / defclass go to the preamble).  Perl's base.pm / parent.pm run inside the `use` = BEGIN.  The obvious fix -- wrap the push in p-BEGIN -- needs a design answer first: %p-begin-situations makes a BEGIN fire at compile time and NEVER at a program fasl's load, so state a BEGIN builds must also exist when a cached compiled program runs (how does today's `BEGIN { push @ISA }` survive a cached run? measure that first: run the probe twice through `pcl` with the cache on).  base.pm also SKIPS a parent the class already isa (parent.pm does not) -- keep the two apart.  Phase/ordering change: the full sweep is the gate, plus the board.
ROWS: Pod-Simple fake-closers.t (7), xhtml20.t (1), xhtml25.t (20) -- counted in the census.

=== RULING s528 (Fable, 2026-10-25) ===
MEASURED (the discriminating probe the filing asked for): `package Bar; BEGIN { push our @ISA, "File::Spec" }` prints `[File::Spec]` on run 1 (the text run) AND on run 2 (the fasl hit) through `pcl` with the cache on -- a BEGIN's effect DOES survive a cached program run.  Mechanism: the script fasl is built at exit by `%p-build-module-fasl` with `*pcl-fasl-build*` bound, under which `%p-begin-situations` answers (:load-toplevel :execute): a p-BEGIN form fires once, at THAT fasl's load, in source order with the declarations around it (cl/pcl-runtime.lisp ~677 and ~28060).  The docstring's "never at fasl load" is the NON-build compile-file case.  So a `p-BEGIN`-wrapped @ISA push needs NO new mechanism -- the filing's design question is closed by measurement.
FIX SHAPE (ruled): `_process_use_base` (and `use parent`) emit the @ISA push -- base.pm's skip-a-parent-the-class-already-isa and parent.pm's `-norequire` kept apart as today -- inside `p-BEGIN` at the statement's OWN source position, i.e. exactly what a user-written `BEGIN { push @ISA, ... }` gets; the require-parent / defpackage / defclass hoists to the preamble stay as they are.  The filing's three probes become the guard rows (a Pl/t file, inverse-verified on a main extraction).
BAR: a phase/ordering change -> the FULL sweep is the gate; corpus-diff explained per file (every `use base` / `use parent` site moves -- expect many files, one explanation); one-file board runs of Pod-Simple fake-closers.t / xhtml20.t / xhtml25.t (28 rows blessed to this task leave the blessed file BY EDIT); everyday; the three artifacts regenerated if any of their sources has a `use base`/`use parent`.
LAYER NOTE (recorded, not for this fix): base.pm is plain Perl, so the end state is `lib/base.pm` + the generic `use` running import at BEGIN time (codegen review C2 closes the `use` text seam); today the parser owns `use base` because the preamble's defclass needs the parent list statically -- noted for C2, not restructured here.
SCHEDULING: a correctness batch after s526w2 merges (it blesses the rows to this task); not for a running agent.

=== DONE (s529b, Opus, 2026-10-31) -- the RULED fix shape ===
Pl/Parser.pm _process_use_base (`use base` + `use parent`) emits the @ISA pushes as ONE `(p-BEGIN (p-push @ISA "P") ...)` in the `definitions` bucket -- the place a BEGIN block's p-BEGIN goes, which Parser2's `sched => 1` route for every Statement::Include interleaves by source position: exactly what a user-written `BEGIN { push @ISA, ... }` gets.  The require-parent / p-defpackage / p-defclass preamble hoists are unchanged; `-norequire` handling unchanged.  SECOND HALF (the filing's probe 2): inside `BEGIN { package MyX; use base ...; }` the push named MAIN's @ISA (the whole BEGIN form is READ in the enclosing section's package; the inner in-package does not apply at read time) -- v1's scheduled-block body now sets `_seam_outer_pkg` to the enclosing package exactly as parse_block_as_function does for a do{}/eval{} body, so `_reader_pkg_differs` qualifies the @ISA symbol.
MEASURED: base.pm's "skip a parent the class already isa" does NOT exist today (both spellings push unconditionally: `use base "F"; use base "F"` -> (F F), perl (F)) -- FILED #4040, unchanged here.
GUARD: Pl/t/use-base-phase-01.t (11 rows; 9 FAIL on main d8577478 -- the filing's three probes, -norequire above the section, a BEGIN after the use sees the parent, `use base` in a sub body, SUPER through a grandparent, the cached program's first AND second (fasl) run; rows 7 and 9 are inverses that were right).
CORPUS-DIFF vs 77c7d9d7: magic.t, method.t, parent.t -- every `use base`/`use parent` site's push moves from the run-time stream into a p-BEGIN at its position (one explanation).  ir-spec §7 normative bullet.
BOARD (one-file runs, tree): Pod-Simple fake-closers.t 7/7, xhtml20.t 1/1, xhtml25.t 20/20 (all three were *FILE* no-TAP rows) -> the three rows left baselines/cpan-board14-fails.tsv by edit; the dist line in cpan-board-dists.tsv carries the file-verdict move.
subject: `use base` / `use parent` pushes @ISA at RUN time at its source position -- perl does it at BEGIN time -- so a call that runs BEFORE the package section (or a `use base` inside `BEGIN { package X; ... }`) sees an EMPTY @ISA: SUPER:: and inherited-through-@ISA lookups fail ("Can't locate object method new via package X"); Pod-Simple fake-closers / xhtml20 / xhtml25
